name: pulse-hemorrhage
title: Hemorrhage and resuscitation in the Pulse engine
description: Three studies on the pulse_hemorrhage and pulse_resuscitation composites, run through the workbench and recorded in each study's runs.db. Their pass criteria are pytest files in each study's tests/ directory, fixed before the canonical runs and after the pilots recorded in workspace/experiments/_runs.yaml.
biological_story: A bleed lowers blood volume, which lowers the blood returning to the heart and so the volume it can pump per beat. The baroreflex senses the falling pressure and raises heart rate, which holds arterial pressure up while the loss is modest. In these runs that compensation kept pressure within 2 mmHg of its start at every sample, and ended within about a millimetre of mercury, up to severity 0.4 (823 mL lost in 10 minutes); beyond that, cardiac output kept falling and pressure followed. Across patients the same bleed removes 1.1 to 1.8 L while starting blood volume spans 2.9 to 7.1 L, so smaller patients lose a larger share of their blood.
question: How does the whole-body Pulse engine respond to a hemorrhage: how does the response scale with bleed severity, does closed-loop fluid resuscitation change it, and does the same bleed behave the same across Pulse's 21 shipped patients?
hypothesis: Blood loss scales with severity while the baroreflex holds arterial pressure until the bleed is severe; a MAP-targeted infusion preserves blood volume and pressure; and every shipped patient compensates the same way, with smaller patients losing a larger fraction of their blood.

executive.what_is_this: Three workbench studies of hemorrhage in the real Pulse whole-body engine.
executive.verdict: All criteria passed (38/38 study tests) on the canonical runs. The criteria were fixed before those runs, from pilots that overlapped them (workspace/experiments/_runs.yaml), except two severity checks added on 2026-10-26 after the runs (every-sample MAP band), which are regression checks.
executive.verdict_detail: Severity: loss and heart rate rise with severity; MAP holds to severity 0.4, then falls. Resuscitation: treatment preserves blood volume and MAP; saline and whole blood add the same volume by Pulse's construction, so volume and MAP barely differ (about 1e-5 after 500 mL). Cohort: every shipped patient compensates; smaller patients lose a larger fraction (rho = -0.91).
decisions_resolved: Run the longer saline-vs-blood follow-up? — Resolved: No (2026-10-26). In Pulse an infusion adds volume at its commanded rate whatever the compound (DrugModel.cpp, IVToVenaCava flow source); the compound only adds its substances. At equal rates saline and whole blood therefore add the same volume, and after 500 mL over 300 s blood volume and MAP were within about 1e-5 of each other (tests/test_processes.py::test_infused_volume_does_not_depend_on_the_compound). A compound comparison needs oxygen-carrying readouts, not a longer run.

scientific_argument.main_claim: Pulse's baroreflex holds arterial pressure against mild bleeds by raising heart rate, and loses it once the bleed is severe.
evidence_for: patient-cohort F-01 (at severity 0.8, every patient raises heart rate and loses MAP)
caveats: One bleed site (RightLeg) and 10-minute runs throughout.
Pulse is deterministic, so each condition is one run.
The cohort criteria and the severity criteria at 0.2 and 0.8 were set after a deterministic pilot of the same configurations.

studies.name: hemorrhage-severity-sweep
studies.title: Hemorrhage severity sweep
studies.question:
How do blood loss, heart rate and mean arterial pressure over 10 minutes
depend on the severity of a right-leg hemorrhage in the StandardMale patient?

discovery_implications.resolved: Over 10 minutes and one site, MAP is defended by baroreflex tachycardia until roughly severity 0.5, then falls as cardiac output drops.
discovery_implications.remaining: Whether the same threshold holds at other bleed sites, over longer windows where compensation may fatigue, and how Pulse severity maps to a calibrated flow rate.

followup_study_proposals.title: multi-site-severity
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Repeat the sweep at a second compartment (e.g. an arm or the aorta) to test whether the severity-0.5 compensation threshold is site-specific.

followup_study_proposals.title: long-window-decompensation
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Extend the severe arms past 10 minutes to see whether the held pressure at mild severities eventually decompensates.

evidence.runs: canonical runs: investigation run of 2026-10-25 at commit b4332d6 (runs.db)

findings.statement: MAP ended at 95.0 and 94.2 mmHg for severity 0.2 and 0.4 (start 95.3), but at 87.9, 84.1 and 78.1 mmHg for severity 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0. Cardiac output at 10 min fell across severities (5.75 L/min with no bleed to 3.95 at severity 1.0), so the heart-rate rise holds pressure only for the milder bleeds.

evidence.runs: canonical runs: investigation run of 2026-10-25 at commit b4332d6 (runs.db)

findings.statement: Severity 0.8 reproduces the earlier reference run (blood volume 3936 mL, MAP 84.1 mmHg); no run reached an irreversible state within 10 min.

evidence.runs: canonical runs: investigation run of 2026-10-25 at commit b4332d6 (runs.db)

findings.statement: Pressure is defended by baroreflex tachycardia, not by reduced loss. Heart rate rises monotonically with severity (71 -> 110 /min) while cardiac output still falls (5.75 -> 3.95 L/min); MAP is held only while the tachycardia offsets the volume loss and breaks once the bleed outruns it (severity >= 0.6). The compensation is Pulse's own cardiovascular reflex, not an imposed term.

evidence.runs: canonical runs: investigation run of 2026-10-25 at commit b4332d6 (runs.db)

studies.claim: Blood loss and heart rate rise steadily with severity, while MAP ends within 1.1 mmHg of its start, and never strays more than 1.8 mmHg, up to severity 0.4 and falls 7-17 mmHg from severity 0.6 upward.

studies.name: fluid-resuscitation
studies.title: Fluid resuscitation after hemorrhage
studies.question:
After a severe right-leg hemorrhage, does a closed-loop MAP-targeted infusion
preserve blood volume and arterial pressure compared with no treatment, and
does the infused compound (saline vs whole blood) matter?

followup_study_proposals.title: Saline vs whole blood on oxygen-carrying readouts
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Pulse adds the same volume for either compound at equal rates (MAP differed by 1.3e-5 after 500 mL), so compare them on hematocrit, hemoglobin and arterial oxygen content instead of running longer.

findings.statement: Untreated: blood volume 3935.8 mL, MAP 84.08 mmHg. Saline: 4014.07 mL, 86.33 mmHg. Whole blood: 4014.07 mL, 86.33 mmHg.

evidence.runs: canonical runs: investigation run of 2026-10-25 at commit b4332d6 (runs.db)

findings.statement: The controller first infused at t = 508 s, when MAP fell below its 90 mmHg target, and delivered 79.6 mL in each treated arm (the rate recorded at t applies over the following second). Saline and whole blood differ by 0.002 mL of blood volume and 0.0006 mmHg of MAP at 10 min; Pulse's own serialized state confirms the Blood arm infused compound Blood.

evidence.runs: canonical runs: investigation run of 2026-10-25 at commit b4332d6 (runs.db)

findings.statement: The improvement is produced by the engineered MapFluidController, not by the fluid itself. The loop watches MAP and commands infusion only once it falls below the 90 mmHg target, so the intervention is late (t=508 s) and small (79.6 mL); the restored volume, not the compound, drives the +78 mL / +2.2 mmHg gain. This is an engineered control term added to the composite, distinct from Pulse's own reflexes. The compound can't matter for volume, because Pulse adds infused volume at the commanded rate whatever the compound (DrugModel.cpp, the IVToVenaCava flow source) and the compound only adds its substances, so at equal rates saline and whole blood add the same volume and differ only in what the fluid carries (repo test tests/test_processes.py::test_infused_volume_does_not_depend_on_the_compound).

evidence.runs: canonical runs: investigation run of 2026-10-25 at commit b4332d6 (runs.db)

studies.claim: Both treated arms end with more blood volume (+78 mL) and a higher MAP (+2.2 mmHg) than the untreated arm, but saline and whole blood are indistinguishable over 10 minutes.

derived.insight: Untreated: blood volume 3935.8 mL, MAP 84.08 mmHg. Saline: 4014.07 mL, 86.33 mmHg. Whole blood: 4014.07 mL, 86.33 mmHg.

studies.name: patient-cohort
studies.title: Hemorrhage across the shipped patients
studies.question:
Does the same right-leg hemorrhage (severity 0.8, 10 minutes) produce the
same qualitative response in all 21 patients that ship with Pulse, and how
does the fraction of blood lost depend on the patient's starting blood volume?

discovery_implications.resolved: Across Pulse's 21 shipped patients the bleed-and-compensate response is qualitatively uniform, and the fraction lost falls with starting blood volume.
discovery_implications.remaining: Whether this holds for a real population rather than Pulse's shipped examples, and whether one severity means the same bleeding rate across body sizes.

followup_study_proposals.title: cohort-no-bleed-control
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Run the no-bleed arm for all 21 patients so the negative control is cohort-wide rather than borrowed from the StandardMale sibling run.

followup_study_proposals.title: severity-calibrated-to-flow
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Map Pulse severity to a per-patient flow rate so equal severity means equal bleeding rate, isolating body size from bleed rate.

findings.statement: In every patient blood volume and MAP fell and heart rate rose. MAP fell by 3.8 mmHg (Bradycardic) to 32.2 mmHg (Joel); heart rate rose by 21.5 (Bradycardic) to 48.9 per min (Rick). No patient reached an irreversible state.

evidence.runs: canonical runs: investigation run of 2026-10-25 at commit b4332d6 (runs.db)

findings.statement: Absolute loss ranged from 1094 mL (ExtremeFemale) to 1755 mL (ExtremeMale), a much narrower spread than starting blood volume (2915 to 7095 mL), so the fraction lost ranged from 23.7% (Overweight) to 37.8% (Underweight); its Spearman rank correlation with starting blood volume is -0.89.

evidence.runs: canonical runs: investigation run of 2026-10-25 at commit b4332d6 (runs.db)

findings.statement: The fraction-volume trend follows from a shared compensation, not from different responses per patient. Every patient runs Pulse's same baroreflex (F-01), and the absolute loss is much less variable (1094-1755 mL) than the starting volume (2915-7095 mL); because a similar absolute loss is taken from very different reserves, the fraction lost falls as starting volume rises (rho = -0.89). The uniform mechanism, not patient-specific physiology, produces the correlation.

evidence.runs: canonical runs: investigation run of 2026-10-25 at commit b4332d6 (runs.db)

studies.claim: All 21 shipped patients bleed and compensate the same way, and the fraction of blood lost falls with starting blood volume (Spearman rho = -0.89).

derived.insight: In every patient blood volume and MAP fell and heart rate rose. MAP fell by 3.8 mmHg (Bradycardic) to 32.2 mmHg (Joel); heart rate rose by 21.5 (Bradycardic) to 48.9 per min (Rick). No patient reached an irreversible state.
